There are two things I propose which may fix a number of the problems we have seen with corruption of moderators and entire communities.

The first one is that users should be able to unsubscribe from individual moderators of a subverse. If a user is not subscribed to a moderator, any actions that moderator takes will not affect that user. For example, deletions of threads or comments. Bans. Also, any moderators that an unsubscribed moderator appoints will by default not be subscribed to without user action. Upon joining a sub, all moderators will be subscribed to by default however.

Beside each moderators name, in parentheses, is the number of people in that sub which are subscribed to them. For example: vac (97%).

In this way, moderators are not all powerful. If they become extremely unpopular, they risk getting unsubscribed from which would render them powerless.

The second proposal is to avoid squatting on a subverse name and creating a community in it which many people don't want. The solution to this is to allow as many communities to share the same name as desired. The original community would have the standard name, such as /v/technology. But then alternates could be created by anyone by using /v/technology/my_alt_name. Every sidebar would (or top bar) would be required to have a link that could be clicked on to view all the alts for that subverse name, number of subscribers in each one, and short description of what it's about.

In this way, a subverse such as /v/GMO could naturally be broken down into inherently pro and anti GMO communities without hijacking the name for only one, and having constant conflict in them. Or, if a community got too arrogant (not just one bad mod, but all of them), then finding all the alt subverses is as easy as clicking on a single link.

I think creative things could even be done, for example /r/theredpill has a whole family of subreddits. They could all be collapsed under /v/theredpill name. For example, /v/theredpill/ask, /v/theredpill/thank, /v/theredpill/becomeaman, /v/theredpill/women, etc.
Some ideas about fixing some of the moderator and community issues

As for the alternate names, what is to stop someone from creating a bunch of alternates but just using them nefariously? Nothing is stopping you from unsubbing from every mod or one mod across many subverses. If that's the experience you want to have, what's the problem? The average user would not be affected.

As for deceptive alternates, I think the pros outweigh the cons. People will get used to the system and understand that the content of the default may have no relation to any of the alts, but conversely, if the default isn't satisfactory, the alts would be a great place to look for alternatives.

And if you were making a nefarious alt, it probably wouldn't have that many subscribers and would be towards the bottom of the list.

In all cases, the casual user wouldn't be generally affected by these features unless they seek them out. They'd probably find out about alts by someone linking to one, as is done with normal subverses. And they probably wouldn't ever unsubscribe from a moderator unless there was some huge drama.

How would this change the simple search algorithm used for finding alternative subs on reddit? IE someone tried to find a sub for avatar the show but the movie has the avatar default subreddit so they search for avatar and boom it's right there in the search because of the description.

Alright, you asked three questions:

  1. You would indeed have free reign and could post anything you wanted, but nobody would ever see anything you posted unless they were also unsubbed from all the mods. And furthermore, none of your posts would ever get upvoted because only 1% of the audience even sees what you posted.

  2. Brigading wouldn't make much sense, because first of all, your subscription to a mod only materially affects what you see. The only thing you could affect would be the number in parentheses next to a given mod's name. And to affect that number, you'd have to be a subscriber to that subverse. Would you really subscribe to something, then unsubscribe from one specific moderator, just to affect a small number next to their name? If it really became an issue, that number could be hidden or removed. But I doubt there would be any targeted brigades because like I said, they couldn't affect another user's experience in any way.

  3. Search has never been great, but I actually see this as helping people find things. First of all, if someone doesn't want their subverse to be prefixed by the name of another one, they shouldn't create it in that location in the first place. Secondly, if you know you're looking for "avatar", then you first go to the root, /v/avatar, and if that isn't what you're looking for, the next logical place would be to look under the alts and see if there is a v/avatar/tv or v/avatar/show in the list. Then at least you'd have a logical place to look for it. Right now, it could be pretty non-intuitive; there is not really a structured place to look if it isn't under /v/avatar like you'd expect.
But then moderators effectively wouldn't be able to remove illegal content.
